ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (dark) pixels with high-intensity (white) regions comprising approximately 25% of the visible surface, creating a high-contrast ratio between the central dark region and lateral light bands.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Broad, contiguous high-intensity horizontal band across the mid-section of the left lobe; dispersed, smaller high-intensity mottling across the mid-to-outer right lobe; uniform low-intensity black pigmentation in the central region and notch area.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, symmetrical V-shaped depression with an approximate pixel angle of 45-50 degrees relative to the lobe midlines; depth extends significantly toward the peduncle.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration pattern across the entire visible margin; distinct jagged peaks and valleys with varied pixel amplitudes; prominent deep notch on the inner trailing edge of the left lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex curvature on the outer distal tips transitioning to a slight concavity approaching the median notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense clusters of high-contrast, roughly circular pixel formations on the extreme lateral tips of both lobes, indicative of barnacle colonization.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, high-intensity linear streaks (rake marks) cutting diagonally through the pigmentation on the left lobe; scattered shorter linear marks visible on the right lobe surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle encrustation on the distal margins; irregular jagged notches on the trailing edge of the left lobe suggesting previous physical trauma or wear.
other_distinctive_markers: High-intensity white pixel clusters and texture indicative of water spray occluding the lower-right margin and basal insertion point of the fluke.
